pr.title: Fix Debug builds: stop PersistenceMode.h from redefining new
pr.body:
Debug builds of `hMailServer.sln` failed with 75 errors in Boost 1.92 headers (`multi_index/detail/node_handle.hpp`, `utility/base_from_member.hpp`). `build\build.ps1` builds Debug by default, so a plain local build broke.

**Cause:** `Common/Persistence/PersistenceMode.h` defined `new` as `DEBUG_NEW`, which expands to `new(_NORMAL_BLOCK, __FILE__, __LINE__)`, for every file that included it. The macro then also rewrote Boost's placement `::new (ptr) T(...)` in any header included afterwards.

**Fix:** remove the macro from the header. The `.cpp` files already define `DEBUG_NEW` themselves after their includes, so debug-heap leak attribution still works.

**Verified:** `build\build.ps1 -Configuration Debug` now builds with no errors or warnings. Release was never affected, and CI builds only Release, which is why this went unnoticed.

Found while working on Phase 1.1 (#9).

commit.message:
Stop PersistenceMode.h from redefining new in Debug builds

PersistenceMode.h defined new as DEBUG_NEW - new(_NORMAL_BLOCK, __FILE__, __LINE__) -
for every file that included it. The macro then also rewrote the placement new
of the headers included after it, and Boost 1.92's multi_index and
base_from_member headers failed to compile: Debug builds of hMailServer.sln
stopped with 75 errors. Release builds, the only ones CI makes, were unaffected.

The .cpp files define DEBUG_NEW themselves after their includes, which is where
it belongs; the header no longer does.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
